stem.text: The mitotic index is a measure of the proportion of cells that are undergoing mitosis in an area of tissue. It is calculated using the formula shown.

stem.latex: \text{mitotic index} = (\text{number of cells undergoing mitosis} \div \text{total number of cells}) \times 100

stem.text: A scientist calculated the mitotic index of areas of onion root at different distances from the tip of the root.

stem.alt: Graph of mitotic index against distance from tip of root in mm, with the vertical axis from 0 to 14 and the horizontal axis from 0 to 2.0, showing plotted crosses joined by straight lines.

A.text: No cell division occurs further than $1.4\,\text{mm}$ from the tip of the root.

B.text: The rate of cell division decreases as the distance from the root tip decreases.

C.text: Most of the cells undergoing cell division are closer to the tip of the root.

D.text: For a sample of 200 cells $0.2\,\text{mm}$ from the tip of the root, 6 would be undergoing mitosis.
